fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Circular Driveway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate it quickly at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the full width of the access drive clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs to allow large emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain an open line of sight from the road to the residence.
• Keep the circular driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so arriving emergency vehicles can pull forward and turn around without reversing back down the long driveway.
• Post the property address visibly at the residence itself, not only at the road, so responders can confirm they have reached the correct structure.
• Identify and communicate a secondary staging area on the open terrain or green space where additional vehicles can park without blocking the driveway or the turnaround.
• Keep the turnaround area of the circular driveway free of planters, decorative boulders, or other fixed obstacles that would reduce the turning radius available to fire apparatus or ambulances.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Brush Area; Scattered Shrubs; Long Driveway; Vegetation Near Structure; Irrigated Landscape; Single Access Route; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Limited Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the house to create open space between the plants and the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the house so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Remove brush from the area closest to the structure, keeping a clear zone of bare ground or short grass immediately around it.
• Cut grass on the open terrain surrounding the house short, particularly during dry periods when it can carry fire quickly.
• Clear overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Remove shrubs and brush growing along the driveway edges that could block vehicle movement or sight lines.
• Separate shrubs and trees near the house so they are not touching each other in a continuous line leading toward the structure.
• Keep the irrigated landscape plants near the house trimmed low and spaced apart so they do not form a dense mass against the walls.
• Clear dead grass and plant material from the brush area nearest the house.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the main road.
• Keep the single access route free of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and debris along its full length.
• Thin shrubs in the open green space where they cluster together and point toward the house.
